question.leadin: Identify some of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: King Nebuchadnezzar ("NEB-uh-kud-NEZZ-ur") of Chaldea ("cal-DEE-uh") built these structures for his wife Amytis ("AM-uh-tis") of Media. They consisted of terraces and irrigation structures that serviced a variety of luscious trees.
question.clue: According to Strabo, an early version of Archimedes' Screw was built for use at this location.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about ancient writing systems.
swap.text: Reeds were used to form wedge-shaped symbols on clay tablets in this writing system, popularized by the Sumerians.
swap.clue: Henry Rawlinson studied the Behistun Inscription for insight into this system, which is seen on the oldest complaint tablet.

question.text: This Mesopotamiam civilization is the earliest known human civilization. This civilization, whose city-states included Ur, developed the cuneiform writing system.
question.clue: A tomb built by this culture contains several ornate lyres, as well as dozens of handmaidens who were sacrificed and buried in a "Death Pit."

swap.text: The Code of Hammurabi was issued from this ancient city on the Euphrates[yoo-FRAY-teez]River.
swap.clue: This city's patron deity was worshipped in the Esagila.

question.text: In their destruction of the city, Mongol forces reportedly caused this river to run black with ink from the House of Wisdom and red from the blood of scientists and philosophers. This river, along with the Euphrates, formed the traditional boundaries of Mesopotamia.
question.clue: This river which flowed through the capital of multiple Persian empires. Along with the Euphrates, this river forms the boundary of Mesopotamia.

swap.leadin: This ancient eastern empire was a vassal state under two large empires during different times of its existence.
swap.text: Name this empire, with capital was Nineveh (NIN-uh-vuh). Its rulers included Sennacherib (suh-NA-kuh-rib) and Ashurbanipal (a-shur-BAA-nuh-paal).
swap.clue: Accounts of invasions by this empire written by king Taharqa record that its armies had their bowstrings eaten by field mice.

question.leadin: This was the first empire of the ancient world.
question.text: Name this empire which reached its peak under Naram-Sin and fell to the Gutian invasions. The Elamites wererivals of this empire.
question.clue: Its most famous ruler's life was detailed on the Ebla tablets, and started out as a cup-bearer to Ur-Zababa of Kish.

swap.leadin: This empire fell to the Medes and the Babylonians in the 610 B.C. fall of Harran.
swap.text: Name this empire, whose capitals included Assur ("ASS-er") and Nineveh. Tiglath-Pileser III instituted numerous reforms in this empire.
swap.clue: The Epic of Gilgamesh was discovered in a library built by one of this empire's monarchs.

question.text: This Assyrian emperor destroyed the city of Babylon and invaded Judah in the Levantine [LEH-vun-teen] War. This son of Sargon II transferred the Assyrian capital to Nineveh [NIH-nuh-vuh].
question.clue: Though he compelled tribute, this ruler was prevented by a plague from capturing Jerusalem from Hezekiah.

swap.text: This capital of the Assyrian Empire contained a massive library established by Ashurbanipal on the bank of the Tigris, and, according to the Bible, it was built by Ashur.
swap.clue: This city was sacked by a coalition including Scythians assembled in 612 BC by the Median king Cyaxares ("kye-ax-AIR-ees"), ending the dominance of a line that included Tiglath-Pileser III.

question.text: Leonard Woolley discovered a "royal" board game in this ancient Sumerian city. This city, which was led by Shulgi during the Sumerian Renaissance, was the site of a Great Ziggurat.
question.clue: A king named -Nammu, who founded a dynasty that supplanted Lagash and the Gutians, was succeeded by Shulgi.

swap.leadin: This man married Amytis, the daughter of the Median King, and Saddam Hussein considered himself the reincarnation of this ruler.
swap.text: Name this Chaldean emperor whose conquest of Jerusalem is depicted in the Book of Daniel.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Nebuchadnezzar</u> II (This is DB, don’t sweat the number here)
swap.clue: Evidence for the Biblical actions of this ruler include a ration list found near the Ishtar Gate which mentions a captive king named Jehoiachin.

question.text: The best example of a Sumerian schoolhouse was found in this city, which was the center of worship for Enlil. This city's Ekur Temple was rebuilt by Naram-Sin.
question.clue: Fragments of Hammurabi's Code have been found in this city, whose "scribal corner" is rich with ancient texts. Various Mesopotamian dynasties sought to control this city of religious importance, the home of the god Enlil.

swap.text: While conducting excavations in Assyria, Layard found many of these statues of winged human headed bulls, which were often found in pairs at the entrances of buildings. Their male counterparts are called shedu.
swap.clue: Several Mesopotamian empires, but most notably the Assyrians, built statues of these protective creatures with a person's face, eagle's wings, and the body of either a bull or a lion.

question.leadin: Objects such as an axe with a copper and gold handle adorned with a boar attest to the influence of these people's culture in Ugarit.
question.text: Name these people whose namesake language was primarily spoken in the Mitanni kingdom.
question.clue: This ethnic group largely made up the population of the Mitanni Kingdom to the southeast of the Hittite Empire. Kikkuli ("kee-KOO-lee") wrote a horse training manual in this ethnic group's namesake language, which was most closely related to Urartian.

swap.leadin: In the thirteenth of lyar he sat upon his throne, and in Tishri he campaigned against the Land of the Two Rivers.
swap.text: Name this re-founder of an empire, who ruled from 745 to 727BCE, beat back the Urartian menace and established a violent military presence in the region. He was succeeded briefly by Shalmaneser V
swap.clue: This ruler's major campaigns included the subjection of Urartu in 735 B.C.E., and the capture of Damascus during the rebellion of Rakhianu.

question.leadin: King Shulgi of Ur built a 150 mile wall to defend against these people.
question.text: Name this Semitic people who established the cities of Ebla and Mari while usurping cities like Kish and Eshnunna. The most famous member of this people conquered Larsa from Rim-Sin I and also instituted a draconian law code demanding "an eye for an eye."
question.answerHtml: Amorites [or Martu; or Amurru; prompt on but DO NOT OTHERWISE MENTION Babylonians]
question.clue: Larsa attained independence from Isin under the governor Gungunum, who was of this ethnicity. Hammurabi belonged to this ethnicity, whose members ruled Babylon before the Kassites and Elamites.

swap.leadin: It was constructed under the order of King Nebuchadnezzar II, and contains many bas reliefs of dragons and aurochs.
swap.text: Name this large blue and gold structure located in Babylon. The walls lining the street leading up to this structure were decorated with a brick mosaic of lions and flowers.
swap.clue: This gate that was once built into the wall that surrounded Babylon. It is named for a deity.

question.leadin: Daniel Fleming discussed "early collective governance" in this polity, which was mostly comprised of Sim'alite and Yaminite tribal confederations.
question.text: Name this polity founded in the early Bronze Age, a major rival of Ebla. "Terrestrial" and "celestial" domains are delineated in a painting from this polity showing a ruler's "investiture."
question.answerHtml: Mari [accept Tell Hariri] (The painting is the investiture of Zimri-Lim.)
question.clue: While providing terminology for parts of the body, animals, and economic functions, the names of specific people are largely absent from a peace treaty between this city and Ebla.

swap.text: Michael Witzel has argued that the BMAC may have left linguistic traces in Sanskrit, Avestan, and the language of this kingdom. This kingdom's elites spoke an Indo-Iranian language and ruled from the city of Washukanni.
